Method of Attack: Using boobytrapped image files with double extensions to hide malicious code that forcibly downloads and installs Locky ransomware
Malicious image files containing JavaScript or HTA code that download and execute ransomware
Malicious SVG files containing JavaScript code that download Nemucod malware and Locky ransomware
Attack Vector: Malicious image files spread via Facebook and LinkedIn social networks
Unsolicited file downloads or clicks on malformed image files in social media messages
Indicators of Compromise: Files with unusual double extensions such as .jpg.js, .jpg.hta
Malicious SVG files with embedded JavaScript
Automatic or user-initiated download of malformed image files from Facebook and LinkedIn
